nobox.final_span:
on Saturday night.
Beyond Lynch, backup Brock Osweiler demonstrated better performance with 180 yards passing. But his pick six from the Jags’ 18-yard line cut Denver’s lead to 7-3.
Whether to run or pass, that results in roughly 20 points per game.
Over the past 11 games, averaging 5.33 yards per play, Denver demonstrates greater running back talent compared to first-round picks — particularly if Jamaal Charles returns to action this weekend following his entire season absence due to a torn left knee ligament.
And, Thomas is returning to life for the stretch run after grabbing seven passes for 150 yards on Sunday.
Now if Lynch can just find a rhythm, Denver’s losing streak since 2013 and early 2015 finishes may be over
